reconcile.note: Gill reads Noah's righteousness as imputed through faith rather than self-earned, so calling him righteous does not conflict with denying anyone is righteous by works.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible sets Paul's flat "there is none righteous, no, not one" against the named figures — Abel, Noah, Job, Daniel, Lot, Elisabeth, Zacharias — scripture itself calls righteous.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Has there ever been a righteous person?"

sides.snippet: I have seen your righteousness before me in this generation.
sides.verseText: Yahweh said to Noah, \"Come with all of your household into the ark, for I have seen your righteousness before me in this generation.

sides.snippet: There is no one righteous. No, not one.
sides.verseText: As it is written, \"There is no one righteous. No, not one.
